correctness.rationale: The Chmieliński functional characterization reduces the optimal reverse parameter for a unit Birkhoff-James pair x perpendicular_B y to min_{g in J(y)} |g(x)|. Dihedral symmetry reduces x to a smooth point (c,t) of one reference edge or its endpoint vertex (c,s). When N is divisible by 4, a smooth x forces y to the perpendicular edge midpoint and gives residual |t|/c<tan(alpha); a vertex x allows exactly the two half-edges around the perpendicular vertex, whose smooth supports evaluate x as plus or minus tan(alpha), while the central vertex has residual zero. The endpoint midpoint gives equality. When N is 2 modulo 4, the perpendicular to a smooth edge is a vertex whose two adjacent supports evaluate x with opposite signs, while the Birkhoff sector of a vertex is one whole edge supported by a functional vanishing on x. Hence every reverse residual is zero.
risks: The proof relies on the exact regular-polygon support geometry; its parity distinction depends on whether the perpendicular radial direction is an edge midpoint or a vertex.
The numerical checker samples the polygonal boundary and is supplementary rather than a proof of the continuum statement.

originality.rationale: The 2020/2021 primary source was inspected at its arXiv metadata and publisher preview, including the C/D approximate-symmetry framing, primary MSC 46B20, and the regular-polyhedral context. It supplies qualitative approximate-symmetry results but no sharp regular-even-polygon formula was found. The 2018 predecessor was inspected at abstract/bibliographic level only; it introduces global approximate symmetry and a related constant, so inaccessible full text remains an explicit residual risk. Targeted indexed searches covered regular-polygon aliases, the exact tan(pi/N) formula, the octagonal value sqrt(2)-1, the dodecagonal value 2-sqrt(3), and the competing Dragomir notion. The closest indexed exact comparison is a regular-octagon Dragomir parameter, which uses a different approximation relation.
residual_risks: The 2018 global-approximate-symmetry paper was not available in full text during this run; an equivalent regular-polygon calculation there would affect originality.
Bibliographic and semantic-index searches cannot establish absolute novelty.
An equivalent tangent formula may be stated under a different name for the optimal C-symmetry constant or only through support-functional geometry.

value.rationale: The result upgrades a qualitative approximate-symmetry theorem to a sharp infinite-family quantitative law. It identifies a clean parity phase transition, supplies the exact optimal parameter for every non-Radon regular even polygon, gives an explicit sharp witness, and quantifies convergence to Euclidean symmetry by chi_C~pi/N. The quantity is intrinsic to the source-defined C-approximate symmetry problem rather than an arbitrary slice.
risks: The theorem is two-dimensional and regular-polygon-specific; no corresponding formula for arbitrary polyhedral planes is claimed.
